screenshots.shows: A single popup as it appears over a game — icon, achievement name, description, and the game line the recent achievements panel adds

steps: Deploy the current build so the shot matches the working tree, not the installed release
python scripts/test-achievements.py backup, then unlock one achievement to fire a real popup
Capture through lib/window-capture.ps1 WITHOUT -CropToOpaque: this popup is translucent by design, so a plain screen grab bakes the wallpaper into it and cropping cannot separate them
python scripts/test-achievements.py restore

screenshots.shows: The system tray context menu: Show recent achievements, Add game, Pause notifications, Settings, Open config/logs location, Report a problem, Exit

steps: Deploy the current build so the menu shown is the working tree's
Right-click the tray icon; poll for the menu rather than assuming a delay, because synthetic right-clicks on the tray open it only sometimes — re-run on failure
Capture the menu window whole; its client area excludes the border, and the border is part of the menu

screenshots.shows: The Settings window on its Notifications page, with the nav rail and the footer visible

steps: Deploy the current build so the shot matches the working tree, not the installed release
Open the tray menu and click Settings...
Select the Notifications page in the nav rail
Capture the client area, not the window: the window rect carries Windows 11's 2px border, which is dark when the OS is in dark mode even though this window is light
Use -CropToOpaque: this window is opaque, so its rounded bottom corners are its own dark border curving into the client rectangle — chrome, which alpha recovery preserves rather than removes

Add the hairline with lib/docborder.py, which the capture script already calls: this window's own edge is near-white (measured 243) and the docs page is white, so the shot has no visible boundary without it. Applied by hand it would be silently lost on the next capture

screenshots.shows: The Add game wizard on its Ready page: the game folder and its Steam AppID, the back-up-the-original-library option with its explanation, the collapsed Advanced options section, and the Back / Cancel / Add game buttons

steps: Deploy the current build so the shot matches the working tree, not the installed release
Open the tray menu and click Add game...

Keep the anchor: the driver points the wizard at a game with a Steam DLL and no steam_settings of its own, so the Ready page shows the ordinary run rather than the 'a configuration already exists' warning. A different game changes what the prose beside the image describes. CAPTURE_GAME_DIR names that game folder and is required: the folder is one machine's install, so the script carries no default
Type the folder into the box rather than using Browse: FolderBrowserDialog is a native modal that blocks the driver thread and cannot be filled by name

Click Next until the button relabels itself 'Add game', then stop. That label IS the stop condition, not a step: pressing it backs up and replaces the game's steam_api64.dll. The driver reads the label before every click and closes the window afterwards, which is the wizard's cancel
Leave Advanced options collapsed: that is the state a user first sees
Use -CropToOpaque: this window is opaque, so its rounded bottom corners are its own border curving into the client rectangle, which alpha recovery preserves rather than removes

Add the hairline with lib/docborder.py, which the capture script already calls: this window's own edge is near-white and the docs page is white, so the shot has no visible boundary without it. Applied by hand it would be silently lost on the next capture

screenshots.shows: The Add game wizard after a finished run: the step checklist, the result line, and the details log open below the Hide details / Close buttons, scrolled to its last line

steps: Deploy the current build so the shot matches the working tree, not the installed release

Build a throwaway 'Example Game' folder under C:/Games holding a copy of a stock Valve steam_api64.dll and a steam_appid.txt of 620 (Portal 2): pressing Add game replaces the DLL, so the run must never touch a real game, and the anchor keeps every library game out of the log
Walk the wizard to Ready, press Add game, and wait for Cancel to relabel itself Close
Click Show details, so the log opens below the buttons; a clean run leaves it closed
Use -CropToOpaque and add the hairline with lib/docborder.py, as for the Ready-page shot
Delete the throwaway folder and restore the installed config.json, which the run's registration can write to
